teams.name: Rogaela State
teams.note: The runners-up lost the title game 47-43 to Costique River in Canesta after beating Leafette, Tasson and Yrei Trobniy on the way, and voters still put them first, 49 first-place ballots. Rami Campbell begins a 17th year, tailback Maisie Althauer went in the first round and quarterback Rohan Chakraborty in the second, and offensive lineman Octavia Danecott and safety Winona Rowden are seniors. They open at home against Rupin State and play North Verigon in week 2.

teams.name: Eona
teams.note: The 2042 champions went 9-5 last year and were knocked out in the second round, 24-21 by Hatesei, after a 55-7 first-round win over German Shores. Receiver Tsuvai Eiselniy was a first-round pick, but cornerbacks Tavesei Roresei, Weimin Labec and Tariq Yawbayo all return, with Alessia Boischamp up front and lineman Tyrell Kingsmond now a sophomore. Hollis Upshaw is in year six and the schedule opens with North Hatesei St at home.

teams.name: Costique River

out.name: Wei Oakcott
out.reason: one shot at a bigger stage

teams.note: The defending national champions, only the second title in school history after 1980, went 15-3 and won the playoff as the 9 seed, beating Dove Island State, Fiota Bay 56-3, Lornaman and Roosevelt 41-38 before the 47-43 final over Rogaela State. Offensive lineman Orivaw Rolaniy was a first-round pick among nine draftees, and sophomore quarterback Radoslav Velecek leads a linebacker group of Doyoon Beom-Sik and Joachim Granmo. Ryo Baker is in year seven, and the road to a repeat starts at home against Waterville.

teams.note: A 6-6 year with no playoff game is the story, and with 21 national titles, the last in 2030, voters have still placed them fourth. Perla Notaro enters year three, only one player was drafted, and the transfer class adds linebacker Catori Wintercott from Marblehead and tight end Faisal Indragiri from Parchynt. They open in week 0 against Crayellan and visit Ranroman State in week 4.

teams.note: A 6-6 season, 3-6 in the Great Fourteen, left them out of the field, and ten players were drafted, including first-round lineman Ximena Coldcombe and second-rounders Taeyang Su-Won and Solene Verfleur at receiver and quarterback. Offensive coordinator Antonella Orellana left to become head coach at Dove Island, and Sybil Inglethorpe arrives from Tengus State to replace her. Boris Walker is in year ten, and the opener is at Milharvey.

teams.name: Kaji Daun
teams.note: The 19 seed lost its first playoff game 35-21 to Leafette after an 8-6 season that included a 7-2 conference record. Safety Alastair Hazelshaw went in the first round, and the offense still has tight end Ziad Anywale, receivers Rupert Goldridge and Kazue Shiranari and lineman Efrain Charbec up front. Henrik Moreau is in year four and the schedule opens at home against Pollard State.

teams.note: They went 7-5, 4-5 in the Great Fourteen, and missed the playoff, with only three players drafted. Litowa Mesteniy returns for a fifth year with redshirt quarterback Dulce Navamayor and senior cornerback Yuma Momose, and the line adds transfers Treiva Yreysei from Hatesei and Nana Chukbayo from Ciarralotta State. Week 3 at Skeenerland State is the first test, and North Hatesei visits in week 4.

Ji-woo Hall begins his 14th year, and the transfer portal brought in six players, including four defensive linemen. Ranroman State visits in week 3 and the trip to Kaji Kita comes a week later.

teams.note: The 2 seed went 13-3 and reached the semifinals, where Costique River beat them 41-38 in the 501 Bowl after a 30-3 quarterfinal win over Reid State. Senior quarterback Haeun Yunye returns with receivers Mele Fenfield and Gerasimos Apovelis, and linebacker Lanying Kawatani is the only draftee. Tane Fifita is in year three, they open at Skylar Rose and visit Hatesei in week 3.

teams.note: A 9-4 season did not reach the playoff, and the staff changes: offensive coordinator Sybil Inglethorpe left for Central Stanton and Hollis Blackford steps into the job. Layla Smith is in year 16 with quarterbacks Tessa Vikstad and Beatrice Peatbourne both back, plus receiver Mireille Grijalva. Cornerback Aurelio Malmont and lineman Ilaria Grijalva were second-round picks, and week 2 is at Pistolheart.

teams.note: The 6 seed won 12 games and reached the semifinals, beating Orlot Western 37-0 and Hatesei 24-17 before Rogaela State won 41-20 at the Redwood Bowl. Defensive linemen Tanisha Ashson and Agnieszka Demedopoulos both left in the first two rounds, but linebacker Rashad Vinter and four receivers return. Hollis Heathcote is in year six, and they open at Ciarralotta State.

teams.name: Hatesei
teams.note: Nine players were drafted, two in the first round, linebacker Sigrid Steindorf and cornerback Imani Greenley, and the 5 seed that beat Eona 24-21 lost 24-17 to Yrei Trobniy in the quarterfinals. They bring in no transfers, so the rebuild runs through senior cornerback Joaquin Lomarini and safety Roviyel Coldfield. Freya Dahlqvist is in year three, and Roosevelt comes to Hatesei in week 3.

teams.name: Skylar Rose
teams.note: The 2041 champions went 8-4 and stayed home after the season, and quarterback Alessia Verville went in the first round. Amir Chen is in year eight with running back Itzel Torrabella and defensive lineman Xiuying Ningshai, and the portal added receiver Ren Hoshizawa from Eona Navy and tight end Sangwoo Ja-Jin. They open at home against Roosevelt.

teams.note: The 2040 champions went 7-5, 4-5 in Broad South, and lost receiver Diamond Woolshaw in the first round and linebacker Padma Devacharya in the second. Bhaskar El-Mahdi is in year four with sophomore quarterback Heriberto Holmhus, senior receiver Anders Osterberg and senior safety Oliver Mayworth. The opener is at home against LSFA, then a trip to Sacred Tomb.

Darnell Ellery is in year five, and quarterback Liesel Nyrud arrives from Wolford with linebacker Nanami Fangzhui and lineman Aoi Rongtuan, while offensive lineman Mingze Zhongyi was a second-round pick. They open at home against UNN and visit Burrstone in week 2.

Ghislaine Penahermosa is in year four and defensive coordinator Urmila Jayawardhan in year 12, with lineman Renshu Yi-Seok and cornerback Tessa Northcombe back. They open in week 0 at Barhold Valley.

teams.note: The 18 seed lost its playoff opener 44-16 to Pistolheart after a 9-4 year, and offensive coordinator Kalani Yellowcrane left to become head coach at Parchynt, with Kiran Goodlow taking over. Imani Latu is in year 18, the longest tenure on this list, with quarterback Winona Manupati, receiver Yaritza Buenaserna and lineman Hollis Thornstead returning. Yrei Trobniy comes to town for the opener.

teams.name: Tasson
teams.note: They went 10-4, beat Skeenerland State 35-20 in round two and lost 24-17 to Rogaela State in the Lumber Bowl quarterfinal, and no one went in the first two rounds of the draft. Andre Hernandez is in year six with defensive coordinator Zuzana Svetecek in year 12, receivers Clive Neubonne and Maelys Marerini, and cornerback Martina Ventimiglia. The schedule opens with Coastal Ranroman at home and Keytommiyr away in week 4.

teams.note: Quarterback Belen Altalarga went in the first round after a 10-4 year in which Marblehead beat Phangrine State 56-27 and lost 43-34 to Roosevelt. Onawa Khan is in year 15 with defensive coordinator Jumana El-Faruqi in year 12, and Gaspard Navafranca is new at offensive coordinator, with junior quarterback Varun Balaraj next in line. Skeenerland visits in week 4.

teams.name: Orlot Western

out.name: Mirae Shanke
out.reason: one shot at a bigger stage

teams.note: The Low Sixteen's best team went 14-1, 9-0 in conference, beat Eona Navy 31-0 and then lost 37-0 to Yrei Trobniy in the second round. Only cornerback Ruben Baldettoni was drafted, and senior quarterback Rosalia Vignatelli, senior safety Ludmila Starenko and senior lineman Ohanzee Vakafusi return, with offensive coordinator Obinna Amasowah in year 15. They open at home against OCU, and the trip to Hansenne comes in week 4.

teams.name: Dietsche
teams.note: A 5-7 season, 3-6 in Jyras Bay, followed the national final of two years ago, and voters are betting on a rebound. Sora Yamamoto is in year six, Ettore Albareal arrives from Barhold at defensive coordinator, and kicker Varun Yongsui and punter Isla Falemaka come from Orlot Western and Southern Krobe. Redshirt linebacker Uchenna Zamorano and lineman Tunde Rowley anchor the defense, and Will Tech visits in week 4.

teams.note: They went 9-5 and won the first round, 44-16 over Ciarralotta State, before Lornaman beat them 41-3, and safety Hollis Elvset left in the first round and lineman Zeyu Rongding in the second. Tage Ludendorf is in year four with junior quarterback Andres Clairlac, and Bora Marettoni is in year one at defensive coordinator. Tengus State visits in week 2 and the trip to UN Ediville follows in week 4.

teams.name: Lornaman
teams.note: The 3 seed went 12-3 and beat Pistolheart 41-3, then lost 41-14 to Costique River in the Steam Bowl quarterfinal. Henry Sandcombe is in year six with sophomore quarterback Joaquin Caldini, Bianca Xanthomakis new at offensive coordinator, and cornerback Sota Oberoi gone in the second round. They open at UN Ediville and host Ekralund in week 2.

teams.note: They went 10-4 and lost 56-3 to Costique River, a Mountain Valley foe, in round two. Catalina Eastwood is in year seven, Bolin Eastwell is new at defensive coordinator, and the portal brought four players, including running backs Frode Rosenhardt and Diego Cabramayor. Sophomore quarterback Sunita Balaprasad returns, and the opener is at Eternal Fox.

teams.note: The 20 seed lost its playoff opener 55-7 to Eona after an 11-3 year, and head coach Antoine Anysei left for Perth Island. Vaiana Sokolov replaces him, hired away from Dove Island State, with offensive coordinator Tsuvai Nosemyr in year nine and defensive coordinator Esteban Monteflores in year six. Senior lineman Barthelemy Longpierre and cornerback Erik Brzezinski return, and the opener is at North Verigon.
